description: MOONIX is a team of innovative minds passionate about AI, space science and technology. We aim to develop an intelligent Lunar Landing Site Navigator using NASA data, interactive lunar maps and advanced analysis to support safer lunar exploration. We welcome developers, AI/ML engineers, researchers and creative thinkers.
summary:
MOONIX is an interactive lunar mission-planning platform that helps users explore potential Moon landing locations and understand how landing dates affect solar illumination and geometric Earth visibility.

Using a 3D lunar globe, four candidate landing sites, Sun and Earth elevation timelines, mission indicators, and date-slip analysis, MOONIX transforms complex lunar geometry into an accessible visual experience.

Users can select a landing site, examine its supported astronomical data, compare locations, and investigate how changing a planned landing date changes the displayed conditions.

Built using React, Three.js, D3.js, Python, SpiceyPy, NAIF SPICE and JPL DE440s, MOONIX aims to support preliminary lunar landing-site exploration and mission-planning education.

It addresses the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge by bringing location, time, illumination and Earth-visibility exploration into one interactive application.
details:
MOONIX — Lunar Landing Site Navigator

The Problem

Lunar landing-site planning involves understanding how environmental and astronomical conditions change with location and time.

Two important factors are solar illumination and geometric visibility of Earth. Their apparent positions relative to the local lunar horizon change over time and can influence preliminary landing-site and mission-schedule analysis.

When a planned landing date changes, mission planners need to investigate whether the conditions at a candidate location also change.

However, interpreting astronomical geometry across multiple locations and dates can be difficult without an accessible visualization tool.

Our Solution

MOONIX is an interactive lunar mission-planning platform designed to make these conditions easier to explore.

It combines a three-dimensional lunar globe, candidate landing-site selection, astronomical elevation timelines and date-based scenario exploration in one interface.

Key Features

1. Interactive 3D Lunar Globe

A three-dimensional visualization of the Moon with markers for the supported candidate landing locations.

2. Four Candidate Landing Sites

Users can explore:

  • Shackleton Rim
  • Malapert Massif
  • Nobile Rim
  • Apollo 11

3. Sun Elevation Analysis

Visualizes the apparent elevation of the Sun relative to the local lunar horizon, helping users investigate geometric sunlight availability.

4. Earth Elevation Analysis

Visualizes the apparent elevation of Earth relative to the local horizon, helping users investigate geometric Earth visibility.

5. Mission Dashboard

Provides elevation timelines, countdown information, illumination indicators and other available mission-planning metrics.

6. Date-Slip Analysis

Allows users to investigate how changing a planned landing date affects the displayed astronomical conditions within the supported data coverage.

7. Preliminary Viability Indicator

Provides a configurable screening indicator to help compare selected conditions. It is not a probability of mission success or a certified landing-safety assessment.

How It Works

MOONIX uses a scientific computation pipeline and a browser-based visualization interface.

The pipeline uses NAIF SPICE infrastructure, planetary ephemeris data and lunar reference-frame information to calculate celestial geometry for supported lunar observers.

Python and SpiceyPy are used in the computation pipeline. Precomputed ephemeris datasets are then made available to the React frontend.

The frontend presents the information through an interactive 3D Moon, D3-based elevation timelines and mission-planning controls.

The general workflow is:

Scientific Data → SPICE Computation → Local Lunar Geometry → Precomputed Datasets → Interactive Dashboard.

Scientific Data Coverage

The current project includes precomputed hourly ephemeris datasets for four candidate locations.

The documented coverage is January 1 through June 30, 2027.

Selected comparisons against JPL Horizons are documented in the project's validation materials.

The application distinguishes scientific ephemeris data from approximate or simulated outputs where applicable.

Technology Stack

Frontend:

  • React
  • TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Three.js
  • D3.js

Scientific computation:

  • Python
  • SpiceyPy
  • NAIF SPICE
  • DE440s
  • Lunar reference-frame kernels
  • JPL Horizons for selected comparisons

Deployment:

  • GitHub
  • Vercel

Benefits and Expected Impact

MOONIX aims to:

  • Make lunar astronomical geometry easier to understand.
  • Help users explore solar illumination and Earth visibility.
  • Enable comparison of candidate landing locations.
  • Support preliminary landing-date investigation.
  • Make scientific information more accessible through interactive visualization.
  • Provide an educational tool for understanding lunar exploration challenges.

Current Limitations

MOONIX is a prototype for preliminary exploration and visualization, not an operational landing-safety system.

Its current ephemeris archive has a limited date range.

Geometric Earth visibility does not establish that a radio communication link will work. Actual communication analysis requires additional RF link-budget and system modelling.

Solar elevation does not establish actual power-system performance.

Detailed terrain obstruction should only be considered where validated terrain elevation and horizon calculations are implemented and available.

The configurable viability indicator is a preliminary screening metric, not a probability of mission success.

Future Development

Future improvements include:

  • Expanded ephemeris coverage.
  • Additional candidate landing sites.
  • Validated high-resolution lunar terrain integration.
  • Terrain-aware horizon obstruction calculations.
  • More detailed communication-link analysis.
  • Solar power-system modelling.
  • Improved uncertainty and data-provenance visualization.
